title: test/system: pass skip_if_aarch64 its message
body:
I was looking at the aarch64 skips and noticed `skip_if_aarch64` reads `$msg`, which it never sets, so the caller's message is dropped. The siblings all do `local msg=$(_add_label_if_missing "$1" ...)` first, this one just doesn't have that line.

There is one caller in the tree and it does pass a message:

```
test/system/520-checkpoint.bats:137:    skip_if_aarch64 "FIXME #28576: selinux problem only on aarch64"
```

so the skip prints the generic default instead of the issue number. Same two functions, arg passed in both:

```
main :  SKIP: Cannot run this test on aarch64 systems
fixed:  SKIP: FIXME #28576: selinux problem only on aarch64
fixed (no arg): SKIP: Cannot run this test on aarch64 systems
```

I used `$1` instead of copying the `_add_label_if_missing` line since that helper says it is for rootless/remote. No CI job runs linux aarch64 at the moment so this only really shows up running the system tests locally on an arm box.

comments.body: @vtushar06 do you wanna add the packit related commit from https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/28565 to this PR and see how it goes?
@lsm5 added it, kept your authorship on the commit:

> Maximum test time '30m' exceeded.

Looks like the aarch runners are to slow and need higher timeouts in the config. Overall I like turning on aarch on tmt since the github action setup cannot offer that at the moment.

@lsm5 all 4 aarch64 jobs errored the same way and its the 30m tmt duration, not a test failure:

```
f43 x86_64    26:20   pass,  815 tests
f43 aarch64   29:59   error, stopped at 751
```

there is no `not ok` anywhere in the aarch64 output, it just ran out of clock, and x86_64 is already sitting only ~4m under the limit so theres no headroom to borrow. the skip itself does work:

```
ok 741 [520] podman checkpoint --export, with volumes # skip FIXME #28576: selinux problem only on aarch64
```

want me to bump duration in test/tmt/system.fmf in this PR, or keep that separate?

> Looks like the aarch runners are to slow and need higher timeouts in the config. Overall I like turning on aarch on tmt since the github action setup cannot offer that at the moment.

@Luap99 yeah agreed, pushed 60m. sizing was the bit I wanted to get right:

```
f43 x86_64    26:20 / 30m   pass
f43 aarch64   29:59 / 30m   cut at test 751 of 815
```

aarch64 was running at ~25 tests/min so it needs ~33m, but x86_64 only had 3:40 spare to begin with, so I went to 60m rather than 40m to stop the same thing biting x86_64 next. duration is a max not a reservation so a fast run still finishes early.
